verses.saheeh: Recite in the name of your Lord who created -
verses.khattab: Read, ˹O Prophet,˺ in the Name of your Lord Who created—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Recite, bring recitation into existence, beginning with: In the Name of your Lord Who created, all creatures;
verses.romanUrdu: Padho (Aey Nabi) apne Rubb ke naam ke saath Jisne paida kiya

verses.saheeh: Created man from a clinging substance.
verses.khattab: created humans from a clinging clot
verses.jalalayn: ﻿created man (al-insān: the generic) from a blood-clot (‘alaq is the plural of ‘alaqa, which is a small quantity of congealing blood).
verses.romanUrdu: Jamey huey khoon ke ek lothdey se Insan ki takhliq ki

verses.saheeh: Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous -
verses.khattab: Read! And your Lord is the Most Generous
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Recite: (reiterating the first one) and your Lord is the Most Generous, having no counterpart in terms of His generosity (wa-rabbuka’l-akram is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject [of the verb] iqra’, ‘recite’),
verses.romanUrdu: Padho aur tumhara Rubb bada kareem hai

verses.jalalayn: ﻿Who taught, [the art of] script, by the pen — the first to write with it was [the prophet] Enoch (Idrīs), peace be upon him —
verses.romanUrdu: jisne qalam ke zariya se ilm sikhaya

verses.saheeh: Taught man that which he knew not.
verses.khattab: taught humanity what they knew not
verses.jalalayn: ﻿taught man (al-insān: the generic) what he did not know, before he was taught, in the way of guidance, [the art of] writing, crafts and so on.
verses.romanUrdu: Insan ko woh ilm diya jisey woh na jaanta tha

verses.khattab: Most certainly, one exceeds all bounds
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay, but verily man is [wont to be] rebellious,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin, Insan sarkahshi karta hai

verses.khattab: once they think they are self-sufficient
verses.jalalayn: ﻿when he sees it, that is to say, his own soul, to be self-sufficient, in terms of wealth — this was revealed regarding Abū Jahl (ra’ā, ‘sees’, means [to see] mentally; istaghnā, ‘self-sufficient’, is the second direct object; an ra’āhu, ‘when he sees it’, is an object denoting reason).
verses.romanUrdu: Is bina par ke woh apne aap ko be niyaz dekhta hai

verses.saheeh: Indeed, to your Lord is the return.
verses.khattab: ˹But˺ surely to your Lord is the return ˹of all˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Surely to your Lord, O man, is the return — [meant as] a threat for him — and so He will requite the rebellious one with what he deserves.
verses.romanUrdu: (halaanke) palatna yaqeenan tere Rubb hi ki taraf hai

verses.saheeh: Have you seen the one who forbids
verses.khattab: Have you seen the man who prevents
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you seen (a-ra’ayta in all three instances [here and below] is an exclamation of wonder) him, namely, Abū Jahl, who forbids
﻿a servant, namely, Muhammad (s), when he prays?
verses.romanUrdu: Jo ek banday ko mana karta hai jabke woh namaz padta ho

verses.saheeh: Have you seen if he is upon guidance
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you considered what if he, the one forbidden, should be upon [a path of] guidance,
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhara kya khayal hai agar (woh banda) raah e raast par ho

verses.jalalayn: ﻿or (aw is for division) be bidding [others] to fear of God?
verses.romanUrdu: ya parhezgari ki talqeen karta ho

verses.saheeh: Have you seen if he denies and turns away -
verses.khattab: What if that ˹man˺ persists in denial and turns away
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you considered what if he, the one forbidding the Prophet, should be denying [God’s guidance] and turning away?, from faith.
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhara kya khayal hai agar (yeh mana karne wala shakhs haqq ko) jhutlata aur mooh moadta ho

verses.saheeh: Does he not know that Allah sees?
verses.khattab: Does he not know that Allah sees ˹all˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Is he not aware that God sees?, what has issued from him, that is to say, He does [indeed] know it and will requite him for it. In other words, ‘Marvel, O you being addressed, at the way in which he forbids prayer, and at the fact that the one being forbidden is actually the one upon guidance, bidding to fear of God, while the one forbidding is a denier, disregarding faith’.
verses.romanUrdu: Kya woh nahin jaanta ke Allah dekh raha hai

verses.uthmani: كَلَّا لَئِن لَّمۡ يَنتَهِ لَنَسۡفَعَۢا بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ
verses.indopak: كَلَّا لَٮِٕنْ لَّمْ يَنْتَهِ ۙ لَنَسْفَعًا بِۢالنَّاصِيَةِ ۙ
verses.transliteration: kalla lain lam yantahi lanasfa'an bialnnasiyati
verses.saheeh: No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock -
verses.khattab: But no! If he does not desist, We will certainly drag him by the forelock—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Assuredly if (la-in: the lām is for oaths) he does not desist, from the disbelief that he is upon, We shall seize him by the forelock, We shall drag him to the Fire by his forelock,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin agar woh baaz na aaya to hum uski peshani ke baal pakad kar usey khinchey ge

verses.jalalayn: ﻿a lying, iniquitous forelock! (nāsiyatin: an indefinite noun substituting for a definite) — the description of this [forelock] in such terms is meant figuratively, and what is actually meant is that individual.
verses.romanUrdu: Us peshani ko jo jhooti aur sakth khatakaar hai

verses.saheeh: Then let him call his associates;
verses.khattab: So let him call his associates
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Let him, then, call upon [the henchmen of] his council, the members of his council (nādin) — a place of assembly where people gather to talk. He [Abū Jahl] had said to the Prophet (s) in reproof, having forbidden him from prayer, ‘You are well aware that there is none in this [town] who has [recourse to] as large a council [of men] as I do. Verily, I shall fill this [entire] valley with mature steeds and young men [in battle] against you if you so wish!’
verses.romanUrdu: Woh bulaley apne haamiyon ki toli ko

verses.saheeh: We will call the angels of Hell.
verses.khattab: We will call the wardens of Hell
verses.jalalayn: ﻿We shall call the Zabāniya, the grim stern angels to destroy him, as [stated] in the hadīth, ‘Had he called his council [of henchmen] together, the Zabāniya would have seized him right before his own eyes!’.
verses.romanUrdu: Hum bhi azaab ke farishton ko bula lengey

verses.saheeh: No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near [to Allah].
verses.khattab: Again, no! Never obey him ˹O Prophet˺! Rather, ˹continue to˺ prostrate and draw near ˹to Allah˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Do not obey him, O Muhammad (s) and abandon prayer, and prostrate yourself, perform prayer to God, and draw near, to Him through obedience to Him.
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin, uski baat na mano aur sajda karo aur (apne Rubb ka) qurb hasil karo
